chunks: And I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who comes to a group of people and claims a house that is in their possession, and he establishes evidence, while the one in whose hand the house is also establishes evidence that he inherited it from his father, and he does not know how its matter was.
So he said: "The one of them with the greater evidence is made to swear an oath, and it is handed over to him."

key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةَ: legal proof or evidentiary support presented in a dispute
key_terms.تُدْفَعُ إِلَيْهِ: is handed over to him as the final legal award
key_terms.دَارًا: a house or property under dispute
key_terms.يُسْتَحْلَفُ: is required to take an oath in judicial procedure

ai.seo_question: How is a house dispute judged in Shia hadith when both parties present evidence?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling concerning a property dispute in which both sides produce evidence. Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام rules that the party with the stronger evidence is to be sworn, and the property is then awarded to him.
